_comment: No active vulnerability bypasses. Format and rules: see README.md here.
Two entries bypassed GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 as 'no patched version exists for
React 18'. Correct when written; already false when removed — the advisory
had been re-scoped, making the pinned react-router 7.18.2 the 7.x patch.
The gate had been passing on its own merits, not on the bypass.
Lesson recorded then: a bypass records a judgement about the world at a
point in time. Re-read before renewing.
── 2026-09-03: five entries drafted, then NOT needed ────────────────────
A sharp -> libvips chain (5 high) was found in tools/netlify-cli after the
gate was widened to audit that lockfile too — it had only ever audited the
repo root, a blind spot on the one tree that runs with production deploy
credentials. Bypass entries were drafted on the reasoning 'no forward fix
exists; npm's only remedy is a major DOWNGRADE to netlify-cli 23.13.5'.
That reasoning was WRONG, and the same lesson caught it a third time. The
advisory patches at sharp >=0.35.0; sharp 0.35.4 was published. The tree
sat on 0.34.5 only because ipx@3.1.1 declares sharp@^0.34.3 — a range, not
an incompatibility. An npm `overrides` entry forces it forward without
touching the netlify-cli pin, and resolved all five. `qs` went the same
way. Both lockfiles now audit clean with NO bypasses.
The generalisable point: 'npm audit fix offers only a downgrade' means the
top-level package has no newer release — NOT that the vulnerable
transitive dependency has no patch. Check the advisory's own patched range
against the registry before concluding a fix does not exist.
Why the override is safe here, and the residual risk, are documented in
tools/netlify-cli/README.md.
